title: Are they giving their best?
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: How do you know when your people are giving you their best?

A student said: when they looked into designing the truck, he draws from past inspiration and other ideas. I said: but he is creating something totally new, so he has no reference. Think how difficult that is.
A student said: the process for obtaining the results he promotes, he does himself. He leads by example. I said: but he can't do it all. He has to rely on other people.

A student said: he has a good indicator of whether somebody is giving 100 percent of their effort, and he doesn't tolerate not getting it. I said: write down the criteria: are the people giving me their best? Are they making excuses? Do they make a decision?
I said: it doesn't matter whether you are right or wrong. The inability to make a decision will stall you at some point. You have to make a decision.

I asked: who knows what momentum is? Mass times velocity. It is a bit of a metaphor, I said. In combat sports like jiu-jitsu it is all about momentum: starting and stopping, timing, when to move and when to stall.

How do you know when you don't have momentum in a company? A student said: when you are not producing anything. I said: you could have no outcomes because you have a problem. Another said: when the outcomes you don't want outweigh the outcomes you do want.
What would you look at today to see if your team has momentum?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write your criteria for a team member giving their best.
Write how you gauge effort without guessing.
Write one decision you have been avoiding.
Write whether your company has momentum, and how you know.
Write the outcomes you don't want that outweigh the ones you do.

check.q: What did a student say about the person's way of leading?
What did I say stalls you at some point?
choices: The inability to make a decision

recap: Know what 100 percent effort looks like. Decide. Check your momentum.
